cells.uncertainty: Four positive-signal C JSON third-party paths pass two valid controls with format-aware tree results, parser source coverage and stable AFL++ feedback: jansson 2.15.1 (282,984 Debian popcon sourcemax installations), json-c 0.19 (269,736), cJSON 1.7.19 (150,958), yyjson 0.13.0 (14,868). Seven Go JSON package paths pass two valid structure-aware controls with parser-source coverage and stable AFL++ feedback: json-iterator/go (18,454 Imported by), tidwall/gjson (10,420), ugorji/go/codec (10,142), goccy/go-json (4,192), bytedance/sonic (2,428), buger/jsonparser (2,171), and valyala/fastjson (895). Pilot cell: ten JSON package/API paths are control-verified and runnable. Jackson databind and core share a tokenizer family; Gson, fastjson 1.x, org.json, fastjson2, json-simple, json-smart, Moshi, and Parsson are separate parser families. Fastjson 1.2.83 has its own DefaultJSONParser/JSONLexer; the com.alibaba:fastjson coordinate adoption metric sums both 1.x and later 2.x fastjson2 facade releases, so it is not a 1.x-only count. Its pinned-release direct-dependent count is separately recorded. Json-simple 1.1.1 is an older 2012 release with a high default-release count, so ranking uses the common deps.dev summed metric. Json-smart is verified on its RFC 4627 object/array mode, not scalar roots. Parsson implements Jakarta JSON-P with its own tokenizer over a local InputStream; the Jakarta API jar supplies interfaces. Three numeric leads remain unverified. Maven Central search is bounded to 100 hits per query (322 unique hits); deps.dev counts measure package adoption, not JSON-specific use. Two valid nested controls do not establish complete format coverage.

Pilot cell: nine high-download package/API paths have valid nested-object and nested-array controls, package parser coverage, and AFL++ feedback; eight parser families are represented. jsonparse (105,362,611 downloads) has no API in its README; Parser.write(Buffer) is evidenced by packaged examples and tests. The adapter requires one root and checks the parser stack and tokenizer state. JSONStream (56,299,470 downloads) is a separate stream API path over the same pinned jsonparse 1.3.1 tokenizer, not an independent engine. JSONStream.parse([]) emits one root according to packaged code and tests despite its README statement. Its private parser exposes no end-of-input completeness check: the adapter requires one emitted root, no error, and stream end, but trailing unfinished syntax after a complete root may go undetected. JSONStream own package source is covered; differential feedback on the valid controls arises only in underlying jsonparse source. @humanwhocodes/momoa (18,038,222 downloads) has a documented string API only: the adapter decodes local bytes as strict UTF-8 and calls parse(text, {mode: 'json'}), which rejects tokens after the first value; the summary is taken from its AST nodes. @streamparser/json receives the entire Buffer and checks trailing bytes after the first root for whitespace. json5 is a JSON5 superset parser with its own lexer and state machine. It parses both valid strict JSON controls exactly through a documented text API, but accepts JSON5-only syntax and its high download count mainly reflects configuration-file use. json-bigint also has a documented string API: the adapter decodes local bytes strictly, then tags the parser's returned tree. Its Crockford-derived parser source is distinct from the other selected families; BigNumber behavior for long numeric tokens is not established by these controls. jsonc-parser adds a strict-option parseTree text API over its own Microsoft scanner/tree parser; both valid controls match but do not test JSONC extension rejection. Other high-download leads remain unresolved. Downloads cover 24 hand-picked candidates, not every search hit. Standard JSON.parse is separate. Two valid controls do not establish complete RFC 8259 support.

Five PHP JSON third-party paths passed valid nested object controls and source-line coverage. Laminas, JSON Machine, salsify and pcrov also passed a valid nested array control and stable source-line AFL feedback. Laminas is abandoned, and its own decoder runs only when explicitly enabled; its default API route delegates to ext/json. JSON Machine shares ext/json for member decoding. salsify accepts only object/array roots and silently accepts concatenated documents, so its harness rejects anything other than one complete document; the tree-building listener is harness code. Two own-parser or partial-own-parser leads remain unverified; five json_decode wrappers are excluded, including colinodell/json5 on both valid controls. pcrov/jsonreader has a separate lexer and state machine, with three parser-source features and AFL tuples differing between the valid controls. The bounded search used five Packagist queries of at most 100 hits each. Package downloads measure overall/historical adoption, not JSON parsing frequency. Valid controls do not establish complete RFC 8259 support.

Nine positive-signal Python JSON third-party paths pass valid nested object and array controls with source-level parser coverage and AFL++ feedback: pydantic 2.14.3 (1,139,429,690 PyPI Stats last-month downloads), jiter 0.19.0 (421,162,504), orjson 3.13.0 (218,014,317), simplejson 4.3.0 (49,365,386), ijson 3.6.0 (46,615,664), msgspec 0.22.0 (39,138,375), ujson 6.1.0 (29,543,889), python-rapidjson 1.26 (4,066,455), and pysimdjson 8.0.0 (679,340). Pydantic embeds Jiter 0.18.0; standalone jiter uses Jiter 0.19.0 through a distinct package API. These are shared-family paths, not independent parsers, and their package downloads are not combined; orjson shares the yyjson C syntax-parser family but this pilot measures its Rust deserializer, not vendored C source lines. ijson uses the asserted yajl2_c backend, with pinned YAJL C tokenizer and Python extension coverage; its source-built embedded YAJL -O0 route differs from the official Linux wheel linkage and optimisation, and its other backends are untested. msgspec uses its own C JSON decoder in _core.c through untyped msgspec.json.decode; its source-built clang -O0 path differs from the official GCC wheel, typed decoding is untested, and JSON decoder sections are counted separately from other codecs in the same file. ujson uses its own UltraJSON C decoder with vendored double-conversion C++ for fractional numbers; both controls equal an exact CPython json oracle tree, and duplicate-key and edge-number behavior is recorded from source, not tested. python-rapidjson parses a local BytesIO stream through rapidjson.load with vendored Tencent RapidJSON v1.1.0-763-g24b5e7a8, the same RapidJSON C++ family as the C++ RapidJSON path at a later revision; RapidJSON reader.h and the rapidjson.cpp wrapper are counted separately, and default number conversion bypasses RapidJSON strtod. PyPI package downloads include non-parse uses and transitive installs. All nine targeted documented leads have been checked; bounded PyPI Simple Index search has not yet been run. pysimdjson uses vendored simdjson 5.1.1 DOM and a generated Cython wrapper; native parser and wrapper source lines are reported separately. Python standard json is separately verified.

Ten verified Rust JSON parser paths selected within the first 100 hits of six crates.io queries (600 hits, 476 unique), captured 2026-11-17. Ten documented leads remain unverified, so this is a bounded pilot rather than a complete top-ten ranking. ijson 0.1.7 was excluded after source inspection: it has an IValue type deserialized through serde_json::from_slice and no own local JSON parser API. Downloads are 90-day adoption proxies that include transitive pulls. Two small valid controls establish only observed RFC 8259 structure; duplicate keys, huge numbers, deep nesting and non-UTF-8 are untested.

Two verified paths from two independent decoder families; no lower-ranked filler entries. Search is a substring match over all Homebrew formula names and descriptions for seven queries, captured 2026-11-17; it misses header-only decoders that are not packaged there. minimp3 and dr_mp3 have no value on the primary metric, so their GitHub stars are recorded as supplemental only and are not compared with Homebrew counts. libmad needs MAD_BUFFER_GUARD (8) zero bytes appended after the input; the harness adds exactly that and counts every recoverable error except the one LOSTSYNC at the guard. Homebrew installs measure macOS/Linux package demand for whole distributions (the mpg123 player and library; the mad formula library), not direct use of the decoding API. libmpg123 is the same engine counted under mp3_id3v2/c, and libmad is the decoder behind the SoX path there. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, or MPEG-2.5 support.

One verified path; no padding. Search is a substring match over all Homebrew formula names and descriptions for six queries, captured 2026-11-17; header-only C++ decoders and vcpkg/Conan packages were not searched. Homebrew installs measure demand for the whole TagLib distribution, mostly as a tag library, not use of its MPEG property API. TagLib parses frame headers and does not decode audio; for CBR streams without Xing/VBRI its duration comes from stream size and the first frame's bitrate. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, or MPEG-2.5 support.

Four verified Go plain-MP3 paths; no padding. Five pkg.go.dev queries were bounded at 100 hits each (313 hits, 242 unique). Three leads remain unresolved and four recorded wrappers or forks share selected parser families. pkg.go.dev Imported by counts package adoption rather than MP3-specific use. The hajimehoshi/go-mp3 and tcolgate/mp3 families are also represented in the tagged MP3 cell; the plain-frame routes are separate format paths, not new cross-cell families. Five pure-Java Layer III paths verified; no padding. jaudiotagger is first-header-only and mp3agic reports only accurate header fields. Both higher-level APIs misidentify the valid 22.05 kHz control start at byte 104 and estimate 5 rather than 12 frames; mp3agic reports 261 ms versus oracle about 313 ms. These paths make no whole-file frame-count or duration claim. JavaMP3 1.0.1 decodes the mono control exactly but crashes on valid 22.05 kHz stereo input, so is excluded with a reproducible probe. Maven Central phrase queries returned no hits, so named leads were inspected via deps.dev and package documentation. deps.dev counts whole-package dependency use, not MP3-specific calls. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, MPEG-2.5 or ID3 behavior. Java SE 25 exports no MP3 reader by inventory.

Five verified paths; no padding. Search is six npm queries of 100 hits each, captured 2026-11-17; downloads were fetched for 15 hand-picked candidates, not every hit. mediabunny was found by `mp3 frame`, `mp3 duration` and `mp3 demuxer`, not the narrower queries. Download counts cover whole toolkits: mediabunny's muxing, conversion and many containers, and codec-parser's AAC, FLAC and Ogg parsers, not MP3 framing alone. The first three remain the highest-download fetched candidates; mp3-duration and mp3-parser have lower adoption. mp3-parser has 40,519 monthly downloads, below the duration-only leads, and is selected for its documented frame reader and exact whole-control walk. Its AFL++ differential is narrow: two source ranges in lib.js octetToBinRep bit extraction, not distinct version/channel branches. None decodes Layer III audio. The mpg123 WASM wrappers are recorded as shared-family leads. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, MPEG-2.5, CRC-protected or ID3 support. No standard Node.js MP3 API exists. codec-parser's valid-control AFL++ differential is narrow: one header-cache range that tracks distinct frame headers, not version or channel branches. Its V8 line counts include module evaluation of imported AAC, FLAC, Opus, Vorbis and Ogg files that audio/mpeg parsing does not call. music-metadata reports MPEG version and layer only through its codec string ('MPEG 1 Layer 3'), not as separate fields, and needs duration: true for a full frame walk. Its valid-control AFL++ differential is 4 sync() tail-policy ranges that track frame length, not version or channel branches. Its V8 package line count (3,539) is mostly module evaluation; MpegParser.js alone is 245 lines. mp3-duration exposes only duration; its count-scoped AFL signal tracks 11 versus 12 frame calls and may reflect input length, not a new branch or line. The same release is also verified for tagged MP3 duration in the ID3v2 cell.

Two verified paths; no padding. Search is seven Packagist search.json queries capped at 50 hits each, captured 2026-11-17; package descriptions alone decided most exclusions. Packagist total downloads count Composer installs of the whole package (and wrappers pull getID3 or Mp3Info transitively), not use of the MPEG frame parser. getID3 reads the first frame header, checks sync on following frames, and derives CBR duration from audio-data bytes and the header bitrate. Mp3Info reads two headers, estimates frames from audio bytes and the computed frame length, and reports duration one frame short ((frames - 1) x 1152 / sample rate). On the MPEG-2 control it uses the MPEG-1 frame-length coefficient, misses the third frame and reads a false sync at byte 236, reporting Layer II 24 kHz mono 96 kbit/s; MPEG-2 is not covered for Mp3Info. Neither path decodes audio. PHP-MP3 (falahati/php-mp3) failed the controls: the v0.9.5-alpha2 tag does not return on PHP 8.5, and the dev-master snapshot reads the MPEG-2 control as 3 frames at 11,025 Hz (data/php/mp3/falahati-php-mp3-control-audit.md). The Zend media reader and fobilow/mp3file are unresolved independent candidates. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, or MPEG-2.5 support.

Three verified paths; no padding. The name search is a substring filter over the PyPI Simple index (serial 43764887) captured 2026-11-17; the 'mp3' and 'mpeg' hit lists were not triaged one by one, and download numbers were fetched only for 13 named candidates, so a less obvious frame parser could be missed. Native wrappers (av, soundfile, audioread, pygame, pymediainfo, miniaudio) are unresolved, not rejected: their parsers are real but outside Python source coverage. eyed3 and pymp3 are unresolved pure-Python leads. Mutagen reads headers and checks frame syncs but does not decode audio; for CBR streams without Xing/Info/VBRI its duration is stream bytes divided by the first header's bitrate. TinyTag also only reads headers: after five equal-bitrate frames it estimates duration from stream size and mean frame length, and it does not expose MPEG version, layer or frame count. Both full-length controls run the same TinyTag lines; its feedback difference is shown with a valid three-frame prefix of the 44.1 kHz control. hachoir is called through its MpegAudioFile class directly, not guessParser, whose fallback tries every hachoir parser in set order. It walks every frame header to EOF and reports version, layer, sample rate, bitrate, channel mode and frame count. It does not decode audio or side information, and its two controls differ by only 4 mpeg_audio.py lines: the MPEG-1 versus MPEG-2 bitrate table and frame-length formula. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, free-format, Layer I/II, or MPEG-2.5 support.

Three verified package paths cover two independent parser families on two valid untagged CBR controls: Symphonia's Rust MP3 demuxer/decoder, reached directly through symphonia-bundle-mp3 and through the symphonia facade's probe and codec registry, and minimp3's C decoder through the Rust minimp3 binding. The symphonia facade is a separate package API over the same Symphonia family, not a new engine. Nine leads remain unresolved, so the verified ranks are not a claim about all MP3 parsers. Search covers the first 100 hits of six crates.io queries (591 hits, 350 unique) captured 2026-11-17; the 'mp3' query alone reports 1119 matches. Recent downloads include transitive dependency pulls and are an adoption proxy, not evidence of direct MP3 parsing use. The two controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II or MPEG-2.5 support.

Pilot cell: three third-party paths (expat 2.10.0, libxml2 2.15.4 and Mini-XML 4.0.6) were built, matched the exact namespace-resolved summary of both valid controls under LLVM source coverage, and have native AFL++ feedback with a stable valid-control differential. They are three distinct parser families. expat leads libxml2 by 6,410 installs (2.2%) on the binary-package metric, a near tie; mxml is two orders of magnitude lower (2,054, 1,842 of them in popcon's no-files column). The Debian sourcemax table would invert the first two (libxml2 source 61,109) only because the libxml2 source now builds libxml2-16 and the older libxml2 binary is no longer attributed to it, so binary runtime-library counts are the primary metric; libxml2-16 (9,413) is not added because hosts may have both. mxml's value is the 3.x soname libmxml1; the pinned 4.0.6 is Debian forky/sid's mxml source, and its libmxml4 binary has no row in the saved snapshot. Mini-XML does not implement Namespaces in XML: it returns prefix:local names and keeps xmlns declarations as attributes, so its expanded names, declaration counts and URIs are computed by the adapter from mxml's tree, not by the package. Popcon counts installations, mostly pulled in as dependencies, not direct parser use. Search was the Conan Center recipe-name substring 'xml' (9 hits, 1 of them a C XML parser) plus seven targeted C names; Conan and Debian miss vendored single-file parsers. The control oracle (controls/xml/check_controls.py) uses Python's pyexpat, the same family as expat but not libxml2 or Mini-XML, so those matches are cross-family checks. The expat harness pins XML_SetHashSalt so AFL++ maps are reproducible; libxml2 and mxml needed no such change. ISO C documents no XML API. Two valid UTF-8 controls without DOCTYPE do not establish DTD, entity, encoding, XML 1.1 or rejection behaviour.

All four C++ XML paths pass the namespace-aware catalog control with source coverage and AFL++ feedback. Xerces-C++, pugixml and libxml++ pass the shared second valid control; TinyXML2 uses a no-processing-instruction variant because it rejects that instruction. libxml++ parser-only feedback and native libxml2 parser.c lines are repeatable and input-dependent. The bounded search covered four named format-specific libraries, so other C++ XML packages remain unmeasured. Homebrew install-on-request orders the first three differently and its libxml++ formula is an older ABI. The libxml++ 275 Debian dev installs sum three ABIs, while its matching ABI-5 package has seven. Two small valid UTF-8 controls cannot establish complete XML 1.0, DTD/entity, encoding or malformed-input behavior.

Seven Go XML package paths pass two valid namespace-aware controls with parser-source coverage and stable AFL++ feedback: etree 2,098; xmlquery 627; mxj 553; beego/x2j 436; govmomi/vim25/xml 163; goxpp 132; gokogiri/xml 108 Imported by. The first four and goxpp use the Go encoding/xml runtime tokenizer through package-specific tree, map or cursor APIs. govmomi/vim25/xml contains its own compiled tokenizer fork of Go encoding/xml; the pinned v0.56.2 package imports no runtime encoding/xml and covers 290 own xml.go lines. Its parser-only AFL feedback differs by 30 fork-source blocks on the valid controls with stable repeats. Its source is a 12,553,438-byte whole govmomi module archive, though the XML package itself is much smaller. Higher-adoption goxml2json (182) and mxj/v2 (178), plus seven other numeric leads, remain unverified; ranks cover selected verified paths only. mxj and x2j map routes lose namespace URIs/prefixes and mixed-content details; x2j byte/string routes alter CDATA whitespace on the valid catalog control, while its selected reader route preserves it. Gokogiri is a cgo DOM binding over pinned libxml2 2.15.4 with 93 Go binding and 1,730 native parser source lines covered; parser-only AFL feedback differs between the controls and is stable over five repeats. Six pkg.go.dev queries recorded 496 hits, 464 unique; the first 100 hits per query were captured where available. Two small valid UTF-8 XML 1.0 controls without DOCTYPE do not establish DTD, entity declaration, non-UTF-8 encoding, XML 1.1, or attribute-value normalization behaviour.

Ten third-party XML package paths are verified and runnable, reaching this cell's ceiling without padding: Jackson XML, Xerces2-J, Woodstox, dom4j, XMLBeans, JDOM2, Aalto, XOM, XPP3, and kXML2. Xerces2-J, Woodstox, Aalto, XPP3, and kXML2 are five independent tokenizer/parser families. Jackson XML projects Woodstox StAX events into Jackson tokens; dom4j, XMLBeans, JDOM2, and XOM build distinct trees over the OpenJDK Xerces SAX fork. Each wrapper has own source coverage and stable parser-derived AFL++ feedback, while underlying parser coverage is reported separately. The standard javax.xml.parsers path is counted separately and shares the Xerces2-J family. Four documentation leads remain unresolved, including legacy dom4j:dom4j; it is not counted beside org.dom4j:dom4j. Maven Central search is bounded to 100 hits per query (345 unique hits); deps.dev summed direct dependents measure package adoption, not XML-specific use or independent tokenizer families. Two small UTF-8 XML 1.0 controls without DOCTYPE do not establish DTD, external-entity, schema, non-UTF-8, or XML 1.1 behavior. kXML2 control and differential results are in its project-scoped receipt and the shared XML aggregates.

Pilot cell: saxes 6.0.0, jsdom 31.0.1, sax 1.6.1, fast-xml-parser 5.12.1, @xmldom/xmldom 0.9.12, xml2js 0.6.2, and xml-js 1.6.11 are control-verified, source-covered, and have input-dependent AFL++ feedback. Comparable 30-day npm downloads rank the seven package paths; counts include transitive adoption. The seven paths cover four independent parser families: jsdom shares saxes and xml2js shares sax. saxes and sax share historical fork lineage but have distinct parser code. fast-xml-parser has its own scanner and validator but no namespace URI resolution, so the adapter resolves expanded names over its qualified names and xmlns attributes. @xmldom/xmldom has its own XMLReader tokenizer and DOM builder, accepts locally decoded text, and the adapter treats every warning or error as fatal. jsdom builds its XML DOM over the same pinned saxes 6.0.0 tokenizer as the selected saxes path; it copies DOCTYPE entity declarations into saxes and forces XML 1.0 rules, and its AFL++ feedback includes input-independent window setup alongside saxes and DOM construction. xml2js and xml-js build distinct trees over the same pinned sax 1.6.1 tokenizer as the selected sax path; it drops comments and processing instructions, which can merge adjacent text segments. Wrapper package and underlying tokenizer source coverage are recorded separately. The search is bounded to recorded queries and snapshot; two valid controls do not establish complete XML 1.0 compliance.

Pilot cell, three verified third-party paths. The earlier zero count wrongly excluded libxml2-family wrappers; PROTOCOL.md lets a wrapper qualify as a package API with its parser family identified, so sabre/xml is counted with family libxml2 (shared with the standard XMLReader path). symfony/dom-crawler was reassessed under the same wrapper rule and counted: its package-own scope is Crawler navigation and XPath/namespace mapping over a libxml2 DOMDocument, not tokenizing, and its Xdebug package lines differ by only one post-parse line between the two controls, so its AFL++ feedback comes from a native overlay (source-built PHP 8.5.12 and libxml2 2.15.4, allowlist limited to libxml2 parser.c/parserInternals.c/SAX2.c and ext/dom document.c plus ext/libxml) running the same Crawler harness, where the controls differ in 357 stable tuples, all arising while addXmlContent parses; its downloads are mostly HTML crawling uses. jms/serializer stays excluded because it maps an already parsed SimpleXML tree onto a target class model. symfony/serializer maps a DOMDocument through XmlEncoder::decode; its Xdebug package lines are separate from 359 stable native parser-time AFL tuples, and its whole-component downloads mostly reflect other encoders. It drops the root name and descendant namespace declarations. The other libxml2-family wrappers (veewee/xml, mtownsend/xml-to-array, saloonphp/xml-wrangler, laravie/parser, orchestra/parser, pear/xml_parser and smaller ones) were not evaluated by the cutoff and remain unresolved, as do the own-code leads prewk/xml-string-streamer and watoki/dom. sabre/xml drops xmlns declarations and text in mixed-content elements by design, so its summary omits namespace declaration counts. Both coverage images use Ubuntu PHP 8.5.4 with libxml 2.15.2; both AFL++ overlays use the source-built PHP 8.5.12 and libxml2 2.15.4. The search covers the first 100 hits of five Packagist queries; controls are two small UTF-8 namespace-aware documents without DOCTYPE. Standard paths: XMLReader::XML, DOMDocument::loadXML, simplexml_load_string and xml_parser_create_ns/xml_parse are four PHP 8.5.12 runtime APIs over the same source-built libxml2 2.15.4, counted separately from the third-party paths and not ranked; DOMDocument::loadXML and simplexml_load_string take the control as an in-memory string, and their AFL++ overlays instrument only libxml2 parser.c/parserInternals.c/SAX2.c plus ext/dom document.c or ext/simplexml simplexml.c. SimpleXML exposes no separate text nodes, so its summary merges mixed-content character data per element (neither control has any); simplexml.c also holds the traversal methods, which the parse-only fuzz target does not call. xml_parser_create_ns/xml_parse is the only push-parser entry point (xmlCreatePushParserCtxt/xmlParseChunk through ext/xml/compat.c's expat-style SAX callbacks, no tree); its summary comes from event handlers with case folding off and a "\x01" namespace separator, the controls go in one final chunk, and its AFL++ overlay instruments libxml2 parser.c/parserInternals.c/SAX2.c plus ext/xml xml.c and compat.c. ext/xml has no comment handler (comments reach the default handler) and reports user-defined entity references unexpanded to the default handler, which the harness rejects.

Six verified third-party paths (lxml, beautifulsoup4, defusedxml, xmltodict, xmlschema and untangle) are selected from nine named PyPI/project-documentation leads. A bounded PyPI Simple Index search remains pending; 3 leads are unresolved, so this is not a completed top-ten ranking. lxml uses source-built libxml2 2.15.4; beautifulsoup4's documented 'xml' builder runs on the same lxml 6.1.3/libxml2 2.15.4 pins (shared parser family, no independent XML tokenizer, recover=True); xmltodict, defusedxml (guarded pure-Python ElementTree XMLParser), untangle (SAX via defusedxml's DefusedExpatParser) and the standard ElementTree path use Expat. defusedxml is a guard facade over CPython ElementTree, not an independent XML engine; its own code is constant on the valid controls, and ElementTree keeps no xmlns declarations, so its comparison with the lxml oracle omits the declaration count. untangle runs SAX without namespace processing and drops namespace URIs; its controls are checked against an lxml oracle projected to untangle's qualified-name view, not against namespace-expanded names. The lxml, beautifulsoup4, defusedxml and untangle controls exercise valid UTF-8 XML 1.0 namespace structures without DOCTYPE, not full XML conformance. PyPI Stats package downloads are not XML-specific use; Beautiful Soup downloads are mostly HTML use, and defusedxml downloads are largely transitive. lxml and beautifulsoup4 AFL feedback excludes parser.c lines 8700-8720 because address-sensitive attribute hash lookups varied across identical valid replays. xmlschema's XMLResource is not an independent XML engine: it consumes CPython's default xml.etree.ElementTree.iterparse events over the C _elementtree parser, pyexpat and Expat 2.10.0. It records xmlns declarations and per-element namespace maps itself, so its controls match the lxml path's full summary including the declaration count; its own 110 lines are the same on both controls and only their hit counts differ. xmlschema downloads are mostly XSD validation use.

Six verified XML parser implementations selected within the first 100 hits of seven crates.io queries (642 hits, 483 unique), captured 2026-11-17. Ten documented leads remain unverified. xml5ever 0.40.0 is an XML5 error-recovering superset parser: the two valid XML 1.0 controls verify namespace-aware output, but it does not establish strict XML 1.0 well-formedness, complete namespace behavior, DTD support, or other encodings. rxml 0.14.0 is a deliberately restricted XML 1.0 parser without DTDs, custom entities or processing instructions, and it rejects comments by default. It parses the shared catalog control exactly but rejects the shared order control (Error(RestrictedXml("comments"))), so its second control is order-default-ns-restricted.xml without that comment and processing instruction. The xml-rs 1.0.0 package is a compatibility re-export of xml and excluded as a duplicate family. Downloads include transitive pulls and are adoption proxies; ranks compare selected independent paths only. RustyXML 0.3.0 passed valid-control parsing but exact repeatable AFL++ feedback was not established; see data/rust/xml/rustyxml-feedback-audit.md.
